slides.title: Move Operations Concept
slides.prompt: Move constructors and move assignment operators transfer ownership of heap memory or resources from a source temporary object into a target object, leaving the source in a valid but unspecified state without copying.

slides.title: Move Constructor Signature
slides.prompt: Fill in the parameter signature for the move constructor of class Vector.

slides.title: noexcept Specifier Importance
slides.prompt: Why is it critical to mark move constructors and move assignment operators as 'noexcept'?
options: STL containers like std::vector require noexcept move operations to provide strong exception guarantees during resizing
The compiler refuses to compile move constructors without noexcept
It automatically frees pointers assigned to nullptr
It forces the compiler to inline the move method execution
slides.correctAnswer: STL containers like std::vector require noexcept move operations to provide strong exception guarantees during resizing

slides.title: Neutralizing Source State
slides.prompt: Fill in the standard value assigned to raw pointers in moved-from objects to prevent double-free errors upon destruction.

slides.title: Move Assignment Self-Assignment Check
slides.prompt: What check must be performed at the start of a move assignment operator (operator=(T&&))?
options: Check for self-assignment (this != &other) to prevent releasing own resources prematurely
Check if the source parameter pointer is non-const
Check if memory is allocated on the stack
Check if reference count equals one
slides.correctAnswer: Check for self-assignment (this != &other) to prevent releasing own resources prematurely

slides.title: Move Assignment Operator Signature
slides.prompt: Fill in the operator signature for class MyArray move assignment.

slides.title: State of Moved-From Object
slides.prompt: According to the C++ Standard Library rules, what condition must a moved-from object satisfy?
options: Valid but unspecified state (can be safely destroyed or re-assigned)
Must be automatically deleted from memory immediately
Must retain its original initial values intact
All pointers must throw exceptions if accessed
slides.correctAnswer: Valid but unspecified state (can be safely destroyed or re-assigned)

slides.title: Default Move Generation
slides.prompt: Fill in the keyword to request compiler-generated default move constructor.

slides.title: Implicit Generation Suppression
slides.prompt: Declaring a custom destructor in a class suppresses the implicit generation of which special member functions?
options: Implicit move constructor and implicit move assignment operator
Implicit copy constructor and default constructor
slides.correctAnswer: Implicit move constructor and implicit move assignment operator

slides.title: std::exchange in Move Constructor
slides.prompt: Fill in the utility function that replaces a pointer value while returning its old value in one atomic step.
slides.codeSnippet:
Buffer::Buffer(Buffer&& other) noexcept 
    : ptr(std::___(other.ptr, nullptr)) {} // Clears other.ptr while returning old ptr
